residency.test: For domestic purposes, an individual is UAE tax resident if physically present 183 days in a 12-month period, or 90 days with UAE nationality, residency or a permanent home plus a job or business.
residency.worldwide_income: There is no personal income tax, so residence matters mainly for obtaining a tax residency certificate under a double tax treaty.
residency.certificate: A Tax Residency Certificate from the Federal Tax Authority is what other countries actually want to see - being physically present is not enough on its own.
residency.warning: Your former home country may continue to treat you as resident. Leaving properly - ending residence there - is the part people get wrong, not arriving in the UAE.

headline.personal_income_tax: none on salary, investment income or capital gains
headline.corporate_tax: 9% on business profits above 375,000, which can reach individuals carrying on a licensed business
headline.social_security: applies to UAE and GCC nationals only

income_tax.name: Personal income tax
income_tax.note: the UAE levies no personal income tax on individuals

employee.name: GPSSA pension (UAE nationals only)
employee.note: 5% for UAE nationals in the private sector; nil for expatriate employees

employer.name: GPSSA pension (for UAE national employees)
employer.note: 12.5% in Abu Dhabi, 15% elsewhere, for UAE nationals only

capital_gains.individuals: no capital gains tax on personal investments, property or share disposals
capital_gains.business_assets: gains realised inside a business subject to corporate tax form part of taxable profit
capital_gains.note: the absence of capital gains tax does not stop your country of citizenship taxing you - US citizens in particular remain fully taxable

quirks: There is no personal income tax, but there is corporate tax. An individual with a commercial licence and turnover above 1m AED from business activity is within the corporate tax net and must register, even as a sole practitioner. Employment income and personal investment income stay outside it.
Free zone companies can qualify for a 0% corporate tax rate on qualifying income, but the conditions are specific and require adequate substance.
The absence of income tax is only half the picture. Housing, schooling and healthcare are typically paid privately and are a large part of the real cost of living.
End-of-service gratuity accrues under the labour law and functions as a form of deferred pay for expatriate employees.
A Tax Residency Certificate requires 183 days of presence supported by entry and exit records, a tenancy contract and bank statements. Apply early - it takes time and other countries will ask for it.

reporting.who_must_file: There is no personal income tax return. Individuals conducting a business or business activity with turnover above 1,000,000 AED in a calendar year must register for corporate tax and file a corporate tax return.

deadlines.what: Salaried individuals have no filing obligation of any kind

deadlines.date: 9 months after the tax period ends
deadlines.what: Corporate tax return for individuals carrying on a business
Corporate tax registration deadline for natural persons who exceeded the 1m turnover threshold in 2025
Economic substance and ultimate beneficial owner filings for certain entities

forms.name: Corporate tax or VAT registration for individuals in business
Corporate tax return, filed via EmaraTax

documents_to_collect: Entry and exit report from the ICP or GDRFA, which evidences days of presence
Ejari or tenancy contract and utility bills
Six months of UAE bank statements for a residency certificate application
Trade licence and audited or management accounts if carrying on a business

penalties.late_corporate_tax_return: 500 per month for the first twelve months, then 1,000 per month
penalties.vat: penalties for late registration, late filing and late payment, each separately assessed

warnings: This model returns zero personal tax, which is correct for salary. It does not compute corporate tax for individuals carrying on a business.
Nationals of the UAE and other GCC states pay social security contributions that are not modelled here.
Moving to the UAE does not end tax liability in a former home country automatically, and never does for US citizens.
